URL: https://news.sky.com/story/unfair-ban-on-drinking-alcohol-in-football-stands-could-be-scrapped-says-burnham-13591266
Sky News — published Thursday 24 September 2026 13:42 BST

NOTE FOR EDITOR: gray-area under the no-sport veto. Core is a PM policy intervention on 1985 legislation, but subject matter is football.

FACTS (Sky News):
- Drinking in view of the pitch has been banned in the top five tiers of men's football since 1985.
- Burnham says the ban is discriminatory and unfair and could be scrapped, possibly on a trial basis.
- Football Supporters' Association welcomed it; UK Football Policing Unit warned it would be "incredibly rash" to change the rules without proper consultation; the EFL said it would be "receptive to discussions".
- Scotland fans will be allowed to buy alcohol in two areas of the Hampden Park concourse for upcoming games, after trials; alcohol has been banned in Scottish stadiums since the early 1980s.

QUOTES:
Andy Burnham, Prime Minister: "I don't think it's fair for football fans to be singled out in that way." / "I think that legislation dates to an era where football was very different, and I do believe there is a case to remove that discrimination." / "There are different ways it could be done, perhaps on a trial basis." / "But I'm not going to back away from what's been a long-held view of mine. I don't see how it can be fair that some supporters of one sport can be treated differently."
Lucy Powell, Education Secretary, to Sky's Sophy Ridge: any change must maintain the "family environment" and "good atmosphere"; "Obviously people can drink at half time. They can drink before the game. There is a lot of alcohol in and around clubs if people choose to drink it. What the prime minister's identified is that in other sports, cricket and rugby and other things, there isn't the same kind of limits on it."
Tom Greatrex, FSA chairman: unfair fans couldn't have a pint "especially since you can sit in the same seat drinking alcohol whilst watching an Oasis gig or rugby league".
UK Football Policing Unit: "Other sports simply don't see the violence and criminal behaviour from their supporters that football does, albeit a minority, with alcohol often playing a significant part in violent and disorderly behaviour."
